stem: The table shows the postwar boom. Michael Harrington's The Other America (1962) challenged the image of postwar affluence by showing which of the following?

options.text: That no American lived in poverty after 1945
options.misconception: Background from the books: Harrington wrote that 40 to 50 million Americans lived in poverty; the book proves poverty persisted.

options.text: That the middle class had disappeared entirely
options.misconception: Background from the books: the middle class grew after the war; Harrington showed poverty beside it, not its disappearance.

options.text: That 40 to 50 million Americans still lived in poverty
That automation had ended all factory work in America
options.misconception: Background from the books: Harrington said automation displaced workers and left them poor; it did not end factory work.

rationales.A: Background from the books: Harrington wrote that 40 to 50 million Americans lived in poverty, so the book proves poverty persisted.
rationales.B: Background from the books: the middle class grew after the war; Harrington showed poverty beside it, not its disappearance.
rationales.C: Background from the books: Harrington counted 40 to 50 million poor Americans, many in city slums and isolated rural towns.
rationales.D: Background from the books: Harrington said automation displaced workers and left them poor; it did not end factory work.
rationales.general:
1. Affluence was real, so the challenge must show poverty beside it.
2. Background from the books: Harrington counted 40 to 50 million Americans in poverty, in decaying city slums and isolated rural towns.
3. No poverty, no middle class, and no factory work all contradict the book.
Remember: A book that challenges a rosy picture does it with a number that will not fit the picture.
